Definition: Agur, a fanciful name for Solomon
BiblicalUsage: Agur is the name attached to the sayings of Proverbs 30: 'The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal.' Tradition has sometimes taken Agur as a fanciful name for Solomon, but the text gives us only the name, his father's name, and the words that follow — thirty-three verses of hard, humble wisdom, ending with the leech's daughters and the four things that are little on the earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Agur's words are worth hearing whoever he was, because they begin where wisdom begins: 'I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.' A man who knows he does not know is the man God can teach.
